html:
SMTO-BOOT-0007 — This installer doesn't support this computer's system

GUID: 9c0006f6-e376-49b4-8272-4d05c1bf8060
Slug: boot-platform-unsupported
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The installer you ran is made for a different operating system or processor type than this computer has, so it stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Use the installer for your system: ./install.sh on Linux or macOS, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh only on a Mac, and src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 for a Gateway on Windows. Each installer only knows how to set up the system it was written for.
  2. For the vLLM model engine installer, use a Linux computer (or WSL2 on Windows) with an x86_64 or ARM64 processor and an NVIDIA graphics card. src/vllm/install-vllm.sh supports only those systems.
  3. If this computer isn't supported, install SMTO on a supported computer and open SMTO from this computer's web browser instead. SMTO runs in the browser, so you can use it here even when it can't be installed here.

What success looks like

  • The installer gets past its system check and finishes with a completion message.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal message, including the Error reference line, note your operating system and processor type, and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit the installer to skip its system check.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The installer's platform or architecture check found no supported branch for this host, for example install.sh's local Gateway step on an OS other than Linux or macOS, src/gateway_macos/install.sh off macOS, or src/vllm/install-vllm.sh outside Linux x86_64/aarch64.

What this means

  • Installer platform/architecture selection has no supported branch for the current host, including a macOS-only installer invoked elsewhere. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Installer platform/architecture selection has no supported branch for the current host, including a macOS-only installer invoked elsewhere.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare host platform/architecture with the chosen installer rather than changing dependency flags blindly.

How to fix it

  • Check uname -s and uname -m and run the matching entry point: install.sh (Linux or Darwin), src/gateway_macos/install.sh (Darwin only), src/gateway_windows/install.ps1 (Windows Gateway), or src/vllm/install-vllm.sh (Linux x86_64/aarch64 including WSL2, with an NVIDIA driver). Do not bypass the check; use a supported host, or set AOR_SKIP_GATEWAY_SETUP=1 for install.sh when the Gateway is installed on another host.
  • Use the supported installer and runtime for this operating system or a supported host.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported matching host and platform installer are used.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
